coverage.target: NFR21.1 — security-design.md §11: the unit writes no audit record; its obligations are that no sensitive identifier leaves the browser (§5) and that every mutation reaches the service through the gateway (§14.1)
NFR22.1, NFR22.2, NFR22.3, NFR22.4, NFR22.5, NFR22.6 — security-design.md §5 and §6

UI-only unit: no Postgres schema or role, no cross-schema read, and no migration. Least privilege at the data layer is the service units' requirement; the only Identity change here is routes on an existing service using its existing repositories (security-design.md §14.1)
NFR24.1, NFR24.2, NFR24.7, NFR24.3, NFR24.4, NFR24.5, NFR24.6 — security-design.md §2, §7, §8, §9
NFR25.1, NFR25.2, NFR25.3, NFR25.4, NFR25.5, NFR25.6 — security-design.md §12 and logical-components.md §1
NFR26.1, NFR26.2, NFR26.3 — security-design.md §12 and logical-components.md §1

performance-design.md §1 and §8: every settings route is a lazy `*Page` module, so the existing `web/scripts/check-size.mjs` route glob and the 150 kB size-limit budget measure it; no dataset ships (T2 uses `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")`), and the unit adds no dependency (T1)

performance-design.md §2 and §5: one D0 read on the entry path with `staleTime: 0`, bounded by `callWithDeadline(…, GATE_DEADLINE_MS)`; a failure is a full-page retry destination, never an unresolved route
performance-design.md §3: `SettingsLayout`/`SettingsNav` read nothing and render from route state; each panel owns exactly one query with its own loading, content and inline-error states

performance-design.md §4: `isPending` flips synchronously on activation so the control disables and the pending label renders in the same frame; mutations keep the app's `retry: false`; the entered value is kept on a failed save

performance-design.md §4 and §6: D3/D2 are single-flight through their own `isPending`, the dialog's confirm is disabled while in flight, a lost answer re-reads D1 rather than assuming success, and `409`/`410` are terminal states, not retries
performance-design.md §3: the recovery banner renders from D1's `recoveryEndsAt`; a `410` on D2 swaps to the terminal view with no second round trip

performance-design.md §5: the app's `shouldRetry` (one retry, `ApiError` `5xx` only) and `mutations: { retry: false }` are used unchanged; no settings route sets `retry`, and the contract's service-to-service clause is explicitly not the browser rule

performance-design.md §3 and §6 plus T6: D1's `404` resolves to `null` through `nullOnNoRecord`, which accepts only the pinned `NO_RECORD_PROBLEM_TYPE`; the sentinel is recorded as a contract dependency (security-design.md §14.4), and `409`/`410` are mapped to states and never retried
performance-design.md §7: D0 sets `staleTime: 0` overriding `createQueryClient`'s 30 s; D3/D2 invalidate `["me","deletion"]` and `["me","account-status"]`; no settings route uses `refetchInterval`

security-design.md §4: every call is same-origin `/v1/...` over TLS to the gateway; the shell's webfont, WalletConnect and Supabase Auth origins are pre-existing and this unit adds none; the timezone list is `Intl`-built so no dataset is fetched

security-design.md §3: the token comes from the shell's in-memory holder; no `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or cookie write; preferences persist server-side (X2); the query cache is memory-only (no persister)
security-design.md §3: the SPA never decodes or validates the JWT; `ProfileView.status` and every other decision come from server reads
security-design.md §3: authorisation travels as a bearer header, so no CSRF token is added — recorded as a decision, not an omission
security-design.md §5: every user-scoped settings route is self-scoped and carries no user id; the one id-bearing path is the export poll, whose opaque job id is ownership-checked and names no person

security-design.md §5: the exact P1 field set is named; `userId` is a cache/key value and is never rendered, logged or put into an error, and the provider subject, hash and ciphertext are never projected

security-design.md §5: error surfaces render `title`, `status` and `correlationId` only; `detail` is never rendered and the shared `ErrorPanel` is not used where it would render `detail`; no error payload reaches analytics
security-design.md §5 and §6: display names render through React's text path with no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; the 1–200 client check is feedback and the server's `422` is authoritative
security-design.md §5: the delete page collects no reason and no free text, so there is no unvalidated input and no personal data in a reason
security-design.md §5: the retained-what text is a fixed i18n sentence plus the server's `retainedCategories`; no category is invented and no retention rule is inferred

security-design.md §2: D0/D1/D2 resolve the caller by auth subject through the stored-record lookup (`find_by_auth_subject`, the shape of `caller_for_deletion`), take no id, and answer only the caller's own status or own open request

security-design.md §2: the five non-denying entry points are enumerated with their bounds; `UserStatus::denies_use` and its `PrincipalService` enforcement are untouched, and a sixth unbounded path is recorded as a security regression

security-design.md §2: each bound is designed and named — no-id self-scope for D0/D1/D2, the `Active → PendingDeletion` edge guard answering `409` for D3, and the ownership check in `deletions.status` for the deletion-status read

security-design.md §1 and §9: server decides, browser presents; the guard and `gateStatus` map are presentational, D0 is re-read on every authenticated entry, and every request is re-decided server-side
security-design.md §9: P2, D2 and D3 are scoped to the caller's own row by the server; no write takes an actor id from the browser, and another user's record answers `404` without disclosure (§7)

security-design.md §8: an explicit `ConfirmDialog` (extended in place, T5) with a focus trap and single-flight; `409` is re-read through D1 and `410` is terminal; the state machine is the idempotency, so no key is needed
security-design.md §8: `recoveryEndsAt` is the server's value rendered exactly through `Intl`; the client never computes the deadline or decides whether the window is open

security-design.md §10: D3 carries a 5/min/user gateway budget declared through the existing `max_requests_per_minute` field on `Route`; the gateway entry and its budget are a recorded dependency (§14.1, §14.3)

security-design.md §10 and performance-design.md §6: a `429` renders as a recoverable inline error with the correlation id, is never looped on, and no mutation is auto-retried so the client cannot amplify it

security-design.md §11: the unit writes no audit record and holds no audit content; its obligations are that no sensitive identifier leaves the browser (§5) and that every mutation reaches the service through the gateway (§14.1)
security-design.md §12 and logical-components.md §1: a labelled `nav` with `aria-current="page"`, one `h1` per route, labelled controls and keyboard order matching DOM order
security-design.md §12: every switch is `role="switch"` with `aria-checked` and a text state beside it, never colour or position alone
security-design.md §12 and §6: field errors are tied by `aria-describedby`; save feedback uses `StatusRegion` and the recovery banner is `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`

security-design.md §8 and logical-components.md §1: `ConfirmDialog` is extended in place (T5) with focus-in on open, a Tab trap, Escape to cancel and focus return to the trigger — one implementation, tested once
security-design.md §12: `StatusPill` pairs each status colour with a word and a dot shape, and the pending-deletion date renders as text beside the pill
security-design.md §12 and performance-design.md §9: jest-axe assertions are part of the unit's Vitest suite for every rendered state, so accessibility fails the build rather than a review
security-design.md §12 and logical-components.md §1: every string exists in EN and VI in the existing `web/src/i18n` catalogues under a new `settings.*` namespace

security-design.md §12: resolution keeps the shell's existing order (`?lang=` → stored preference → browser → English); the panel edits the stored preference through X2 and renders the server's per-field `source` rather than re-deriving it (T3)
security-design.md §12 and §8: every date and number goes through `Intl` in the profile locale and timezone; the recovery date is an exact formatted date, never a bare relative string
